content: 1. The metabolism of ethinylestradiol can be influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Mineral oil reduces the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance remains unclear. 3. Ethinylestradiol may enhance the effects of naratriptan through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 5. Ethinylestradiol may reduce the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of adverse effects. This interaction is observed with nortriptyline, protriptyline, and amitriptyline. The mechanism is unspecified, and the clinical significance is unknown. 6. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 7. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Rosuvastatin increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is uncertain. 9. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of both norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Acitretin reduces the effects of norethindrone through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 11. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially impairing glycemic control in diabetic patients. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Concomitant use of ethinylestradiol and aminocaproic acid may result in additive hypercoagulability due to increased clotting factor production and platelet aggregation by estrogens, and inhibition of fibrinolysis by aminocaproic acid. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of caffeine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Concomitant use is not recommended. Non-oral contraceptive methods should be used. 17. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while carbamazepine reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use may lead to contraceptive failure. Alternative methods of contraception are recommended. 18. Antibiotics such as amoxicillin, ampicillin, cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, and cefuroxime may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women using oral contraceptives should consider additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control methods. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Bosentan reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 21. Brigatinib reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use may result in decreased contraceptive efficacy and fetal harm. Women should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 22. Butabarbital reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 23. Belzutifan reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Women of reproductive potential should use effective non-hormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 24. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of bendamustine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism, potentially increasing plasma concentrations of bendamustine. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Armodafinil reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 26. Artemether/lumefantrine reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
